object_description: low cell-like building with a strongly recessed attic
design_condition: The low building alternates between the orientation of the surrounding high-rise slabs and the rotated primary school, forming a shared courtyard and a connected sequence of landscaped outdoor spaces.

positive.statement: The building fits comfortably into the existing context through geometric references that alternate depending on the scale.
The new shared courtyard forms an attractive counterpart to the primary schoolyard.
The flowing green space is transformed into a diversely structured environmental design.
The weather-protected entrances are combined inside to form an open hall with a clear vertical organization.
The open ground-floor meeting area can be divided when necessary.
The cell structure is cleverly used for the school clusters.
The classic room layout can be converted into integrated group-room units or open learning landscapes.
The contribution offers a convincing solution for school operations through its spacious ground floor, flexible clusters and roof library.
The facades create a beautiful play of light depending on the sunlight.

negative.statement: Whether the divisible open meeting area works acoustically is questionable.
Rooms with light on three sides are judged difficult to furnish.
More attention should be paid to structural wood protection.
The large floor areas and building volumes mean that high construction costs can be expected.
